v.q: What is Inversion of Control in Spring?
o: The container creates objects and supplies their dependencies
Objects call the container to start the JVM
Beans are created in reverse alphabetical order
v.w: You declare what a class needs, and the container wires it. Dependency injection is the main way IoC is applied.

v.q: Which statement about Inversion of Control is NOT true?
o: The class creates its own dependencies
v.w: IoC means control moves from the class to the container.

v.q: What is the default scope of a Spring bean?
o: Singleton: one shared instance per container
Prototype: a new instance per injection
Request: one instance per HTTP request
v.w: Singleton beans must be stateless or thread-safe, because many threads use the same instance.

v.q: Which scope creates a new instance each time the bean is requested?
v.w: Prototype gives a new instance per injection or lookup. Singleton is the default.

v.q: A singleton bean injects a prototype bean via the constructor. How many prototype instances does the singleton see?
o: One, created when the singleton itself was built
A new one on every method call
One per thread that uses the singleton
v.w: Use `ObjectProvider<T>`, `@Lookup` or a scoped proxy to get a fresh prototype each time.

v.q: How do you get a fresh prototype on every call inside a singleton?
v.w: Injection happens once, so ask the container each time you need a new one.

v.q: Why is constructor injection preferred over field injection?
o: Dependencies are explicit and final, and the class tests easily
It is the only way in which Spring can inject any bean
Spring does not support field injection at all
It makes every bean in the container prototype scoped
v.w: Constructor injection also reveals when a class has too many dependencies, a hint it is doing too much.

v.q: Which statement about field injection is NOT true?
v.w: Constructor injection is the one that makes dependencies explicit.

v.q: Two beans implement `PaymentGateway`. Injecting `PaymentGateway` fails with `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException`. How do you fix it?
o: Mark one `@Primary` or select one with `@Qualifier`
Delete one of the two interfaces
v.w: You can also inject a `List<PaymentGateway>` or a `Map<String, PaymentGateway>` to use all of them.

v.q: Which annotation selects a bean by name when two implementations exist?
v.w: @Qualifier picks a named bean. @Primary marks the default.

v.q: Two beans depend on each other through constructors. What happens at startup?
o: Spring fails with a circular dependency error
Both beans are created without a problem
Spring creates them lazily on demand
One of the beans is silently ignored
v.w: Circular constructor dependencies cannot be resolved. Redesign by extracting a third bean or using events. Boot 2.6+ disables circular references by default.

v.q: Which fix removes a circular dependency between two beans?
v.w: A cycle usually shows two classes sharing a responsibility, so extract a third class.

v.q: What is the order of a typical bean lifecycle?
v.w: `BeanPostProcessor`s run around initialisation. That is where proxies for `@Transactional` and `@Async` are created.

v.q: Which callback runs just before a bean is destroyed?
v.w: @PostConstruct runs after injection. @PreDestroy runs at shutdown.

v.q: What does `@Configuration` with `@Bean` methods let you do?
o: Define beans in Java, even for third-party classes you cannot annotate
Replace the Maven dependencies declared in a project
Run SQL scripts against the database at startup
Create REST endpoints automatically for every bean
v.w: `@Component` stereotypes work for your own classes. `@Bean` is for objects that need custom construction.

v.q: Which situation needs a @Bean method instead of a stereotype annotation?
v.w: You cannot add @Component to library code, so declare it in a configuration class.
